content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text evaluates a pressed link after both sides answered it, so K-C governs whether the collision is weighed chain against chain by footing rather than verse by verse.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "‘never verse by verse’ — one reading permits a judge to declare an individual verse underdetermined by its own ambiguity; the other requires resolving the collision by chain-against-chain footing rather than by the single pressed verse.", "why": "The judge text rests its UNDERDETERMINED finding on Matthew 1:16’s own admitted ambiguity instead of weighing the competing chains’ footing, which is the verse-by-verse inquiry K-C retires."}
